messages:
alex chen: paging: monitoring alerts spiking for US-WEST-2 (az-b) healthchecks — Route53 reports ~30% failures across probes starting ~17:42 UTC. lots of noise, sending raw logs to thread.

oncall-rotation-bot: @alex chen you are the current oncall for eng-sre. escalation level: P2.

alex chen: quick check — curl against the probe target returns 502 from the internal LB in az-b: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://10.3.21.45:8080/health` -> `502`. logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection`.

sam roberts: looking at routing table in az-b, I see a recent ASG rebuild from the deploy window that bumped some instances behind the LB into a different port group. possible probe endpoint mismatch. pulling terraform state now.

jordan lee: can you paste the Route53 healthcheck config? suspect TTL/endpoint drift between monitoring inventory and actual targets.

alex chen: pasted config: ```json
{"Type":"HTTP","ResourcePath":"/health","IPAddress":"10.3.21.45","Port":8080,"FailureThreshold":3}
```

sam roberts: confirmed — monitoring inventory (mon-inventory-prod) thinks target is 10.3.21.45:8080 but the LB config was updated to forward to 10.3.21.45:8081 during the ASG rotate yesterday. probed both ports: 8080 -> 502, 8081 -> 200.

alex chen: okay that explains the 502s. this is a monitoring config drift, not a network fabric problem. but traffic to customer endpoints routed through az-b may see degraded responses while healthchecks mark endpoints unhealthy and route53 fails over. need quick mitigation: update healthcheck target to 8081 or revert LB, or disable failing healthchecks to stop flapping while we roll a fix. comments?

mira patel: taking this incident. I'll coordinate with network ops and infra. immediate plan: 1) disable the specific Route53 healthcheck to stop alerting, 2) patch mon-inventory and rotate healthchecks to 8081, 3) coordinate a small canary to ensure we don't mask a real application failure. I will accept pager.

oncall-rotation-bot: @mira patel is now on-call and has acknowledged the incident.

mira patel: executing step 1 — disabling healthcheck id hc-azb-1203. command: `aws route53 disable-health-check --health-check-id hc-azb-1203` (run by infra-runner). I'll keep the ticket updated.

network-bot: Note: observed routing changes during ASG rebuild at 2024-11-09T17:10:05Z for az-b. No BGP flaps.

sam roberts: while healthcheck is disabled I'll update the monitoring inventory: replacing port 8080 -> 8081 for host 10.3.21.45 in mon-inventory-prod (PR: github.com/redwood/mon-inventory/pull/412). suggest to apply only to az-b slice first.

alex chen: rolling the PR to patch inventory in az-b now — starting with canary of 5 hosts. watch logs: `kubectl logs -n monitoring health-checker-canary` shows success on 8081.

mira patel: customer impact note: per our synthetic telemetry, approximately 0.6% of user-facing requests experienced elevated 5xx rates between 17:42 and 17:54 UTC; affected surface was primarily US-WEST-2 az-b and some cross-region routed sessions from APAC that briefly hit az-b. No active SLO breaches for majority of customers but several VIP customers in APAC reported increased error rates. I've opened INC-34567 and flagged for account teams.

jordan lee: created the incident ticket INC-34567 with tags: `region:us-west-2`, `az:az-b`, `component:route53-healthchecks`, `impact:partial`. Assigning network and infra owners.

mira patel: mitigation completed — mon-inventory PR merged and applied to az-b slice, healthchecks updated to 8081, re-enabled checks after canary: `aws route53 enable-health-check --health-check-id hc-azb-1203`. Monitoring shows steady success for 5 minutes.

alex chen: follow-ups: 1) investigate why LB port change wasn't reflected in inventory (deploy automation gap), 2) add CI assertion to validate healthcheck targets against LB forwarding rules before ASG swaps, 3) add automated rollback to disable healthchecks only if we detect config mismatch.

mira patel: handing off to jordan for post-incident tracking — I will be off shift in 20m. Jordan, please take on the postmortem and customer comms draft.

jordan lee: taking ownership. I'll draft a customer-facing blurb and coordinate postmortem. action items assigned in INC-34567.

alex chen: quick note for oncall book: when you see a cluster of Route53 healthcheck 502s, check LB forwarding rules and inventory mapping before assuming network fabric issue. save us some paging noise. :face_with_head_bandage:

mira patel: thanks team. marking this thread for follow-up during postmortem. closing monitoring alerts for now. :white_check_mark:
